newsitem.title: USA: Summit wives enjoy Rocky Mountain heights.
newsitem.headline: Summit wives enjoy Rocky Mountain heights.

text.p: While world leaders at the "Summit of the Eight" in Denver discussed high finance and world problems, their wives took a train trip to the majestic Rocky Mountains on Saturday.

"Let's do a chorus line," suggested first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton, with Naina Yeltsin on her right and Aline Chretien to her left, as they posed for photographers at 10,700 feet (3,300 metres) with a breathtakingly beautiful view of the Continental Divide behind them.

Chretien, wife of Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien, tried to pitch in with a modest can-can kick, while Yeltsin, Russian President Boris Yeltsin's wife, laughed heartily. A bluegrass band played nearby to welcome the women.

Most of the wives were casually dressed in pantsuits, although Flavia Prodi, wife of Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Kamiko Hashimoto, wife of Ryutaro Hashimoto, the prime minister of Japan, wore skirts.

After a group picture -- in the same protocol formation as their husbands -- the wives walked slowly into a lodge at the Winter Park Resort, a ski area owned by the city of Denver, about 65 miles (100 km) from Denver.
The whole affair was carefully scripted, except when the official Kremlin photographer, walking backwards to get just the right picture, tripped into a flower bed. Only his ego was hurt.

Square dancers entertained the women during their lunch of layered spring vegetables, honey and walnut-smoked shrimp and chicken, manchego tamale tart, passion fruit with fresh cherries and glazed kumquats.

On a two-hour train trip across the Continental Divide -- a great north-south ridge along the Rockies that separates rivers flowing west from those flowing east -- the first ladies heard about the area from local historian Tom Noel.

In a scene recalling the whistle-stop tours that were once the staple of American political campaigns, the wives waved from the open-air deck of the caboose to people gathered in Tolland, a ghost town.
Details of what the first ladies talked about on the train were not available.
Did lawyers Hillary Clinton and Cherie Blair, wife of new British prime minister Tony Blair, swap lawyer jokes? "They might have. I wasn't party to them," said Clinton spokeswoman Marsha Berry.

The wives of French President Jacques Chirac and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl were not on the trip. The party included Rita Kok-Roukema and Daniele Binot Santer, wives of top European Union officials.
